entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Battle of Dorylaeum was a pivotal event in the history of the Crusades, occurring on July 1, 1097, in Dorylaeum, Anatolia, as a decisive victory for the Crusader army led by Bohemond I against the Seljuk Turks. This battle marked a significant turning point in the capture of Nicaea and the subsequent march towards Constantinople, shaping the trajectory of the First Crusade and the medieval history of the region.

The Crusaders, numbering around 1,200 knights and 800 infantry, clashed with the Seljuk forces, estimated to be between 20,000 to 50,000 soldiers. The Seljuk army, led by Kilij Arslan I, suffered heavy losses, with many of their soldiers killed or wounded. The Crusaders, on the other hand, emerged victorious, having secured a crucial victory that would allow them to continue their march towards Constantinople.

The legacy of the Battle of Dorylaeum can be seen in the eventual capture of Nicaea in 1097 and the subsequent Crusader conquest of Jerusalem in 1099. The battle also marked the beginning of a long and complex relationship between the Crusaders and the Byzantine Empire, with significant implications for the politics and culture of the region.

As Seljuk historian Ibn al-Qalanisi noted, 'The Franks, who had arrived in Anatolia, were victorious and their leader, Bohemond, became famous for his bravery and cunning.' The Battle of Dorylaeum remains a significant event in the history of the Crusades, marking a turning point in the capture of Nicaea and the subsequent march towards Constantinople.
